```
===== SKILLS =====
--- skills/epic-run ---
name: epic-run
description: Orchestrate a whole Epic from the Claude Code CLI. The MAIN agent follows this skill (subagents can't spawn subagents) — resolve Story dependency order, run each ready Story's Loop Prompts via the story-loop-runner agent, commit per Story in one Epic worktree, close out each Story, then epic-closeout opens ONE PR PER PHASE against the current branch. Entry point: `/goal Execute WOS-<n> epic plan and run all loop prompts in the plan & sub stories in sequence`.
--- skills/epic-closeout ---
name: epic-closeout
description: Close out an Epic -- roll up all story reviews into an Epic summary doc, update milestones and inventory, open a final Epic PR, then invoke post-epic-closeout to verify cross-refs and resolve the tracking issue.
--- skills/post-epic-closeout ---
name: post-epic-closeout
description: After an Epic closes -- verify and refresh cross-references (PR/issue numbers, frontmatter, plan rows) using lint/grep, then use LLM judgement to close or partially-close the tracking issue.
--- skills/story-review ---
name: story-review
description: Review Story output against acceptance criteria, changed files, tests, docs/inventory, and evidence. Read-only; does not claim completion or write the review doc.
--- skills/story-final-review ---
name: story-final-review
description: Generate docs/stories/wos_<n>_review.md from a Story's validation matrix. Use at Story end, after every Acceptance/Test check has reported PASS/FAIL/SKIP. Mirrors the prior Story's review layout — does not invent metrics.
--- skills/worktree-story-pr ---
name: worktree-story-pr
description: Execute the worktree-end git+gh sequence — commit (one per Loop Prompt), push the worktree branch, open a PR against the current integration branch. Used by story-closeout (standalone Story) and epic-closeout (one PR per Epic). Use only after the review doc is written.
--- skills/plan-dashboard ---
name: plan-dashboard
description: Use to refresh the Delivery Plan Dashboard (GitHub issue #144) — edit the manifest, re-render, and sync the issue body in place (never a comment). Triggers include "refresh issue #144", "refresh the plan dashboard", and /plan-dashboard.

===== AGENTS =====
--- agents/epic-closeout ---
name: epic-closeout
description: Use during/at the end of an epic-run to close out a completed PHASE (or the whole Epic). Per phase, writes the phase review + handoff and opens ONE PR for that phase against the current integration branch; at Epic end writes the Epic roll-up review (docs/plan/wos_<n>_review.md) + handoff and updates docs/plan/README + the Epic file. Never merges.
--- agents/story-closeout ---
name: story-closeout
description: Use after every Loop Prompt in a Story has reported PASS. Writes docs/stories/wos_<n>_review.md + docs/handoffs/wos_<n>_handoff.md, updates the Epic's Stories table + docs/plan/README, and commits the Story (one commit per Loop Prompt). Under an epic-run it does NOT open a per-Story PR — the epic-closeout opens one PR for the whole Epic.
--- agents/story-loop-runner ---
name: story-loop-runner
description: Use to execute ONE Loop Prompt from a Story file (docs/stories/wos_<n>_<slug>.md). Reads the shared story-loop-protocol + the Story's Loop Prompt, runs the scoped work, reports PASS/FAIL/SKIP inline, stages changes. Does NOT close out the Story (story-closeout) or commit/PR.
--- agents/story-reviewer ---
name: story-reviewer
description: Use to review a Story against its acceptance criteria and the Loop Prompts, and produce a structured review report. Read-only; never claims completion on its own.
--- agents/reviewer ---
name: reviewer
description: Use proactively after code changes, test runs, or validation runs to review the evidence and recommend continue/revert/stop.
--- agents/implementation-planner ---
name: implementation-planner
description: Use proactively before implementation to produce scope, assumptions, files likely to change, test plan, risks, and acceptance criteria. Read-only planning.
```

Central reference for every `WOS_*` runtime override in this repo. Convention: settings written
as `${WOS_*:default}` (or shell `${WOS_*:-default}`) are overridable at runtime via environment
variables; unset/empty falls back to the inline default. Tracked in **issue #149** (Claude Code
harness inventory).

> **Precedence (CI workflows):** `workflow_dispatch` input → repo variable (`vars.WOS_*`) → built-in default.

### Using-Discussions.md (when to use) ###
## When to use what

| You want to… | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Ask "how / why / is this expected?" | **Discussion › Q&A** | Answerable, searchable; not a work item |
| Float a feature / scope idea | **Discussion › Ideas** | Gauge interest before it becomes an epic |
| Get a quick group decision | **Discussion › Polls** | Lightweight vote |
| Share something you built / a demo | **Discussion › Show and tell** | Visibility & knowledge-sharing |
| Capture meeting notes & follow-ups | **Discussion › Meeting Notes** | Durable record; easy to evolve into an Idea/Issue/Poll |
| Broadcast a release / heads-up | **Discussion › Announcements** | Maintainers post, team subscribes |
| File actionable, ownable work | **[Issue](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/issues)** | Tracked to closure with an owner |
| Record durable orientation | **This Wiki** | Long-lived, human-facing |
| Record a canonical decision/spec | **[`docs/`](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/tree/main/docs) (ADR)** | Versioned with code |

Rule of thumb: **conversation → Discussion; commitment → Issue; canon → `docs/`.**

## Categories

- 📣 [Announcements](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/announcements) — updates from maintainers.
- 💬 [General](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/general) — anything that doesn't fit elsewhere; introduce yourself here.
- 💡 [Ideas](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/ideas) — propose features/scope before they become epics.
- 🗳 [Polls](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/polls) — take a quick vote.
- ❓ [Q&A](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/q-a) — ask for help; answers can be **marked as accepted**.
- 🙌 [Show and tell](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/show-and-tell) — demo what you made.
- 📝 [Meeting Notes](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/meeting-notes) — notes from meetings (decisions, action items, follow-ups).

### About Meeting Notes
Post one thread per meeting (title `YYYY-MM-DD — <topic>`). Capture decisions
and action items, then **evolve each follow-up into the right home**:

- an actionable task → **Create issue from discussion**
- a proposal to explore → **[Ideas](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/ideas)**
- a decision to settle → **[Poll](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/discussions/categories/polls)**, then land the outcome as an **ADR** in [`docs/decisions/adr/`](https://github.com/noobill/work-os-rebuild/tree/main/docs/decisions/adr)

`@`-mention owners on each action item so follow-up is unambiguous.

## Handy features

- **@mention teammates** — type `@username` to pull the right person in (e.g. ask a question and `@`-mention the code owner). Mention a whole team with `@org/team`.
- **Mark an answer (Q&A)** — the author/maintainers can mark the reply that resolved it; the thread then shows as *Answered* and is easy to find later.
- **Create issue from discussion** — when a discussion (or a meeting action item) turns into real work, use **⋯ → Create issue from discussion** to spin up an issue that links back to the thread (no copy-paste, keeps the trail).
- **Reference in a new/existing issue or PR** — paste the discussion URL, or type `#` to autocomplete and cross-link. Cross-references show up on both ends.
- **Convert issue ↔ discussion** — maintainers can **convert an issue to a discussion** when it's really a question/idea, not tracked work (and vice-versa via "Create issue from discussion").
- **Link a PR** — mention the discussion in a PR body so reviewers see the context; mention the PR in the discussion when you ship the answer.
- **Reactions & polls** — 👍 to signal agreement without noise; Polls for a countable decision.
- **Pin / lock / mark as duplicate** — maintainers keep the board tidy: pin evergreen threads, lock resolved ones, mark duplicates.
- **Subscribe** — watch a category (or the repo's Discussions) to get notified; unsubscribe from noisy threads.

## Etiquette

- **Search first** — a Q&A answer or meeting note may already exist.
- **One topic per thread** — easier to mark answered and to reference later.
- **Title for search** — write the title as the question ("Why does X redirect to Y?"), not "help".

> ## PART 1 — The two loop skills `dev-plan` and `dev-loop`
> 
> Both are Claude Code skills under `.claude/skills/`. They are a **matched pair**: `dev-plan` produces the plan/spec (and optionally an implementation-readiness handoff); `dev-loop` consumes that handoff to implement. Both use an **autonomous, read-only Codex CLI reviewer** (`gpt-5.5`, `reasoning_effort=xhigh`) where **Claude writes/fixes and Codex only audits** — Codex emits `audit.json`, and the orchestrator (Claude) publishes the audit comment on its behalf.
> 
> ### `dev-plan` (`.claude/skills/dev-plan/SKILL.md`)
> - **Purpose:** turn a feature request source into a reviewed planning/spec PR with registered epics/stories, a tracking issue, and a bounded external review loop.
> - **Invocation:** `/dev-plan <issue:N|pr:N|N|path-to-spec-or-zip> [mode=impl]` (`disable-model-invocation: true` — slash/explicit only). First arg mandatory; bare number resolves PR-first-then-issue.
> - **Inputs:** a GitHub issue, PR, plain spec file, or `.zip` request pack; repo planning conventions (`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/plan/README.md`, `docs/stories/README.md`, `docs/context/index.md`); live registries.
> - **Outputs / artifacts:**
>   - Epic docs `docs/plan/wos_<n>_<slug>.md`, story docs `docs/stories/wos_<n>_<slug>.md`, updated plan/story READMEs, OD/ADR entries.
>   - One planning/spec PR; at-most-one tracking issue per epic.
>   - `mode=impl` only: per-story `docs/stories/<slug>.readiness.json` (conforms to `docs/harness/schemas/implementation-readiness.schema.json`) + epic side-product `docs/stories/<epic-slug>_work_advice.md`.
>   - Interview scratch `temp/<yyyyMMdd>_<slug>_spec_<lang>.md` (gitignored, default `zh`); committed docs in `en`.
>   - Runtime state `.dev-plan/state/<source>.json`; per-run artifacts `.dev-plan/artifacts/<run_id>/` (`latest` symlink).
> - **End-to-end steps:** resolve source → find optional dashboard → collect context → triage scope (exit early for small/complete/non-feature) → gap analysis → interview (decision table, one/small batches) → draft/refine epic+stories → `[mode=impl: Step 7b readiness pass — DoR gate → READY_FOR_IMPL or stays DOC_ONLY]` → open/update tracking issue → open/update ONE planning PR → **Codex review loop** (post audit before fixing, append per round) → fix/rebut (`fix-disposition.json`) → closeout at `READY_FOR_MERGE` (human-merge default).
> - **State machine:** `DISCOVER_SOURCE → TRIAGE_SCOPE → COLLECT_CONTEXT → ANALYZE_GAPS → INTERVIEWING → SPEC_LOCKED → DRAFT_PLAN_DOCS → [IMPL_READINESS] → OPEN_OR_UPDATE_SPEC_PR → SYNC_TRACKING_ISSUE → REVIEWING ⇄ FIXING_OR_REBUTTING → READY_FOR_MERGE | WAITING_FOR_HUMAN | SPEC_REWORK → DONE | EXITED`.
> - **Two finish lines:** default = `READY_FOR_MERGE` of `DOC_ONLY` design-freezes; `mode=impl` carries finalized stories to `READY_FOR_IMPL` (the contract `/dev-loop` consumes — solves the handoff gap in issue #178).
> - **Dependencies:** Codex CLI (or GitHub Action / OpenAI Responses API / manual) reviewer backend; the dev-loop skill downstream; optional Playwright MCP (off by default); optional read-only DB (`SUPABASE_DB_URL`→`SUPABASE_DB_URL2`).
> - **Config knobs:** `.dev-plan.yaml` (falls back to `CONFIG.example.yaml`). Key `${WOS_PLAN_*}` overrides: `max_review_turns` (5), `max_question_batch` (5), `base_branch` (main), `allow_auto_merge` (false), `allow_db_read` (true), `interview_language` (zh), `reviewer.model` (gpt-5.5), `reviewer.effort` (xhigh), `approval` (never), `sandbox` (read-only). Structural keys (`docs.*`, patterns, markers) are fixed.
> 
> **`dev-plan/CONFIG.example.yaml`** — full documented default config: `schema_version 1.0`; blocks `loop`, `state` (gitignored `.dev-plan/`), `branches` (base main, human-merge default, branch patterns `feat/{feature_abbr}-wos-{epic_number}`, `temp/{owner_or_agent}/{slug}`), `source_resolution`, `docs`, `tracking` (dashboard search by title keywords "Delivery Plan Dashboard"/"kanban" + labels `delivery-plan`/`planning`), `planning` (incl. `impl_readiness` DoR rows: code_deliverables, testable_acceptance_criteria, definition_of_done, validation_commands, zero_open_decisions, buildable_status), `reviewer` (codex-cli, `codex_github_action` disabled, `pro_audit` gpt-5.5-pro disabled), `security` (db_env_vars, `env_files: [.vscode/.env]`, forbidden_outputs), `github` (round-specific audit markers), `human_gate`, `merge`, `validation` (npm run docs:check / inventory:audit / inventory:map / ci:local).
> 
> **`dev-plan/schemas/`** — `audit.schema.json` (dev-plan external audit output), `decision.schema.json` (OD-*/ADR-* ledger), `fix-disposition.schema.json` (fix/rebut disposition).
> 
> **`dev-plan/scripts/`** — `resolve-source.sh` (resolve arg to one source), `find-plan-dashboard.sh` (locate optional dashboard issue), `collect-context.sh` (gather planning context), `validate-plan-docs.sh` (registry structural checks), `render-tracking-issue.py`, `render-pr-body.py`, `render-codex-command.py` (render Codex cmd, no exec), `run-codex-review.sh` (run autonomous read-only review), `classify-audit.py` (audit.json → routing token), `render-readiness.py` (emit + DoR-gate readiness artifact), `resolve_config.py` (load `.dev-plan.yaml` w/ `${VAR:default}` expansion), `scan_secrets.py` (single secret-safety gate), `publish-status-comment.sh` (post status/round PR comment).
> 
> **`dev-plan/templates/`** — `interview_spec_en.md` / `interview_spec_zh.md` (interview decision tables), `implementation_scope.md` (readiness scope), `tracking_issue.md`, `planning_pr_body.md`, `codex_review_prompt.md`, `claude_fix_prompt.md`, `audit_comment.md` (marker `<!-- dev-plan-audit r{round} -->`), `closeout_comment.md`, `work_advice.md`.
> 
> ### `dev-loop` (`.claude/skills/dev-loop/SKILL.md`)
> - **Purpose:** drive a locked target through implementation → local validation → PR → autonomous Codex review → fix/rebut → fresh review → merge readiness. Implementation only, not planning.
> - **Invocation:** `/dev-loop <issue:N|pr:N|N|WOS-epic|WOS-story[,...]|path-to-task-file>` (also `disable-model-invocation: true`). Resumable from `.dev-loop/state/<slug>.json`, PR, issue, branch, prior artifacts.
> - **Inputs:** the target + `.dev-loop.yaml` (single source of truth). **Prefers the dev-plan handoff** `docs/stories/<slug>.readiness.json`; if a story is `DOC_ONLY` / has no readiness artifact it **stops and recommends `/dev-plan <target> mode=impl`**.
> - **Outputs / artifacts:** code + tests; the PR (body from `templates/pr_body.md`); `validation.json`, `audit.json`, `fix-disposition.json`, `browser-evidence.json` under `.dev-loop/artifacts/pr-<pr>/r<round>/`; state `.dev-loop/state/<slug>.json`; PR audit + fix-disposition comments (round-specific markers, append never overwrite); tracking-issue/dashboard sync.
> - **State machine:** `TARGET_RESOLVED → SCOPE_VALIDATED → IMPLEMENTING → LOCAL_VALIDATION → PR_OPENED → READY_FOR_EXTERNAL_REVIEW → EXTERNAL_REVIEW_RUNNING → FIXING_OR_REBUTTING → FIX_VALIDATION → READY_FOR_HUMAN_MERGE → MERGED` (↘ `WAITING_FOR_HUMAN` / `BLOCKED`). Every review/fix bound to exact `head_sha`; HEAD change ⇒ stale evidence.
> - **Steps:** resolve target → find dashboard → collect context → reject/redirect unsuitable work → classify work-kind → **lock scope** (`validate-scope.py`, exit 20/21 ⇒ redirect `/dev-plan`) → implement (drive locked scope as a `/goal`) → local validation → request Codex review (`codex exec --ask-for-approval never --sandbox workspace-write --output-schema … --output-last-message …`) → classify audit → fix/rebut/defer → loop to `max_review_turns` → merge readiness (human-merge default) → stop conditions → final report.
> - **Reviewer difference vs dev-plan:** dev-loop Codex runs `sandbox=workspace-write` + `network_access=true` (so it can run `gh`/DB/browser evidence and write `audit.json`), but `repo_write_policy=forbidden` and `enforce_no_diff_after_review=true` reverts/invalidates any audit that leaves a worktree change. `danger-full-access` refused either way; reviewer never commits/pushes/comments.
> - **Config knobs:** `.dev-loop.yaml` with `${WOS_DEVLOOP_*}` overrides (see Part 2).
> 
> **`dev-loop/schemas/`** — `audit.schema.json` (Codex review round output, one per pr/round/head_sha), `fix-disposition.schema.json` (Claude's per-finding disposition), `loop-state.schema.json` (resumable state at `.dev-loop/state/<slug>.json`), `review-target.schema.json` (resolved target).
> 
> **`dev-loop/scripts/`** — `resolve-target.sh`, `find-plan-dashboard.sh`, `collect-context.sh`, `classify-work-kind.py`, `validate-scope.py` (scope-complete + zero-open-decisions gate), `run-local-validation.sh`, `run-codex-review.sh` (enforces no-diff + HEAD), `classify-audit.py`, `render-audit-comment.py`, `publish-pr-comment.sh`, `sync-tracking-issue.sh`, `sync-plan-dashboard.sh` (delegates to repo `scripts/plan/sync-dashboard.mjs`), `browser-evidence.sh` (Playwright-MCP UI evidence), `verify-head-sha.sh` (stale check, exit 3), `resolve_config.py`, `lib/config.sh`.
> 
> **`dev-loop/templates/`** — `pr_body.md`, `codex_review_prompt.md`, `claude_fix_prompt.md`, `audit_comment.md`, `fix_disposition_comment.md`, `review_request.md`, `tracking_issue_update.md`, `closeout_comment.md`.

> ## PART 3 — Epic / Story mode (vs milestone mode)
> 
> ### Terminology decision (key point for your tracking issues)
> Per `docs/engineering/story-loop-protocol.md`, **"milestone" is deliberately NOT the delivery unit** — it is reserved for the runtime/architecture concept (One Agent milestone model, Plan Gates). The top delivery unit is an **Epic**, sliced into **Stories**. (Historically renamed: `milestone-review`/`milestone-reviewer` → `story-review`/`story-reviewer`, 2026-06-10.) A legacy "Cycle"/`CNNN_SNN` scheme was migrated to `WOS-N`. Your own repo's memory uses "milestone mode" (`docs/milestones/mN/…`, loop-prompts, final-review); this repo has **no `docs/milestones/` dir** — it replaced that with epic/story mode. The GitHub workflow file `milestone-review.yml` is a separate unchanged CI artifact.
> 
> ### Layout & naming
> - **Epics:** `docs/plan/wos_<n>_<slug>.md` (one file per epic) + `docs/plan/README.md` registry (Epics table) + GH milestone. Century-block story numbering (WOS-100 → wos_101…109; WOS-500 → wos_501…512). Also `docs/plan/wos_<n>_review.md` (epic closeout roll-up), `wos_1_audit_register.md`.
> - **Stories:** `docs/stories/wos_<n>_<slug>.md` + `docs/stories/README.md` registry. Per-story companions: `wos_<n>_review.md`, `docs/handoffs/wos_<n>_handoff.md`, `wos_<n>.readiness.json` (dev-plan→dev-loop handoff), `<epic-slug>_work_advice.md`.
> - **Keys:** single global monotonic key `WOS-N` (type stored as metadata, not baked into number). Display ID e.g. `WOS-124 [Story] — …`. Filename = snake_case key + slug. Story frontmatter carries `parent: WOS-<epic>`. Branch `feat/wos_<n>_<slug>`.
> - **Frontmatter relationship metadata** (Jira-like): `parent`, `children`, `related`, `github_issues`, `github_prs`, `dependencies`, `blockers`, `external_links`, `docs`, `evidence`, `attachments` (referenced as links/paths, never pasted).
> - **Templates:** `docs/engineering/templates/epic.template.md`, `story.template.md`, `story_handoff.template.md`, `story_review.template.md`, plus `closeout.template.md`.
> - **Manifest/dashboard:** `docs/plan/dashboard.manifest.json` → rendered into **GitHub issue #144** ("Delivery Plan Dashboard", live board `orgs/noobill/projects/1`) by `scripts/plan/sync-dashboard.mjs` (workflow `.github/workflows/plan-dashboard.yml`, skill `/plan-dashboard`). Separately, the harness inventory tracker is issue **#149**.
> 
> ### Readiness ladder (`implementation_status` frontmatter)
> `DOC_ONLY` (design-freeze; `/dev-loop` refuses, redirects to `/dev-plan`) → `READY_FOR_IMPL` (buildable; set by `/dev-plan mode=impl`, emits `wos_<n>.readiness.json`) → downstream `TEST_PROVEN`, … (set by `/dev-loop`). `ai:ready`/`decision:confirmed` remain human labels. (Issue #178 = the handoff contract.)
> 
> ### Skills & agents in the epic/story lifecycle
> Skills (`.claude/skills/`):
> - **epic-run** — MAIN agent orchestrates a whole epic: resolve story dependency order (topo-sort), readiness-gate (READY/SKIP/BLOCKED), one epic worktree, delegate each Loop Prompt to `story-loop-runner`, commit per story, then `epic-closeout` opens **one PR per phase**. Entry: `/goal Execute WOS-<n> epic plan…`.
> - **epic-closeout** — roll up story reviews into epic summary (`docs/plan/wos_<n>_review.md`) + epic handoff, update plan README + epic file + inventory, open final epic PR, invoke post-epic-closeout. Never merges.
> - **post-epic-closeout** — verify/refresh cross-refs (PR/issue numbers, frontmatter, plan rows), then close/partially-close tracking issue.
> - **story-review** — review story output vs acceptance/tests/docs/evidence; read-only, doesn't write the review doc.
> - **story-final-review** — generate `docs/stories/wos_<n>_review.md` from the validation matrix (after every check PASS/FAIL/SKIP).
> - **worktree-story-pr** — commit (one per Loop Prompt) + push worktree branch + open PR against integration branch; used by story-closeout (standalone) and epic-closeout.
> - **plan-dashboard** — refresh dashboard issue #144 (edit manifest, re-render, sync body in place).
> 
> Agents (`.claude/agents/`):
> - **story-loop-runner** — execute ONE Loop Prompt; report PASS/FAIL/SKIP; stage changes; does NOT close out or commit/PR.
> - **story-closeout** — after all Loop Prompts PASS: write review + handoff, update Epic Stories table + plan README, commit story (one commit/Loop Prompt); under epic-run does NOT open per-story PR.
> - **story-reviewer** — review story vs acceptance + Loop Prompts; read-only.
> - **epic-closeout** (agent) — per-phase review+handoff and one PR per phase; at epic end writes roll-up review+handoff; never merges.
> - Supporting: `reviewer`, `safety-guard`, `requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team`, `legacy-archaeologist`, `implementation-planner`, `issue-triage-agent`, `pr-review-followup`, `release-readiness-agent`, `context-source-of-truth-agent`, `inventory-drift-auditor`, `test-coverage-reviewer`.
> 
> ### Loop Prompt format
> Each Loop Prompt = one scoped independently-committable task with fields: `Task`, `Acceptance`, `Test`, `Files (likely)`. One commit per Loop Prompt; run its test before moving on. Loop Prompts expanded lazily at pickup.
> 
> ### GitHub labels / conventions (`.github/labels.yml`)
> - **Types:** `type:feature` (Stories), `type:bug`, `type:drift`, `type:test-gap`, `type:decision`, `type:docs`, `type:cleanup`.
> - **AI/decision gates:** `ai:triage`, `ai:ready`, `ai:implementing`, `ai:blocked`; `decision:needed`, `decision:confirmed`. (Stories need `ai:ready` + `decision:confirmed` before AI implements. Under epic-run a planned epic/story *implies* `ai_ready` via frontmatter — set `ai_ready: false` to hold; gate keys on deps-met + concrete Loop Prompts + not-blocked.)
> - **Priority:** `priority:P0/P1/P2`. **Areas:** `area:frontend/supabase/auth/docs/testing/config/inventory/release/runtime/harness/skills/platform`.
> - Story = GH issue `type:feature` with `parent:` epic; Epic = GH **milestone**. PR closes the issue. Dashboard labels: `delivery-plan`, `planning`; waiting labels `agent:needs-human`; auto-merge label `agent:auto-merge-ok`.
> 
> ### Milestone-mode remnants
> No legacy `docs/milestones/` delivery docs remain (that pattern was replaced). "Milestone" survives only as (a) the runtime concept in `docs/architecture/flow_milestone_model.md`, `wos_600_..._milestone_b.md`, and (b) GH milestones per epic (`wos-1`, etc.). The story-loop-protocol has a "Backward compatibility (legacy cycle scheme)" section mapping Cycle→Epic, `CNNN_SNN`→Story `WOS-N`.

> ### Protocol doc

# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/milestones/m*/loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

# kaggle-code-agent Milestones

Status: M0–M10 done; M11 PARTIAL (T000–T006 + T008 done 2026-06-09; T007 deferred pending human action); M12 ✓ done (T007 real-submit DEFERRED); M13 ✓ done (eval/reliability/regression suite — 34 PASS / 4 SKIP / 0 FAIL); M9.2 ✓ done (/save-log operator-tooling skill); M14 ✓ done (goal-driven Kaggle workflow — 21 PASS / 3 SKIP / 0 FAIL; T008 live PASS-WITH-DEVIATION: 2 real pushes, 0 LB scores via the push≠submit gap #77; follow-ups #77 #78); post-M13 work: M11-T007 + M12-T007 unblock + M13.1/M13.2 follow-ups; M15 next (submit step #77; cross-account quota #21; FK hardening #60)
Created: 2026-05-16
Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform

## Product thesis

`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.

Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.
Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.

The platform should help a human user:

- discuss ideas and strategies;
- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.

Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.

## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.

### 1. Platform-development coding agents

These are external AI tools used to build this repository.

Examples:

- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.

Role:

- write and review this product's source code;
- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
- run local tests and CI repair loops;
- open branches/PRs under human supervision.

# M14 — Loop Prompts

_Goal-driven Kaggle workflow: turn the platform from "one approved push" into
"set a goal, explore in parallel, push within Kaggle's rules, poll smartly,
escalate when stuck."_
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M10 exit confirmed (notebook-submission path validated;
see `docs/milestones/m10/final-review.md`). M11 (CTF), M12 (Devpost), M13 (eval
suite) are NOT prerequisites._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle / Anthropic
outside designated paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, per-milestone worktree
by default, secret denylist, Discovery / Debate Gate on `arch:` tasks)._

---

## M14 at a glance

M14 lifts the platform from M10's single-shot, human-approved push to a
**goal-driven Kaggle loop**: declare a target up front, fan out candidate
experiments locally, screen them by holdout CV, push the survivors to Kaggle
under per-competition concurrency limits, poll their kernel runs with adaptive
cadence + batched status reads, write LB scores back to the DB, and either
(a) iterate to the next batch when below goal, or (b) escalate to a human when
the idea well is dry.

The five user-surfaced bullets from PR #44 each become a numbered task in this
milestone, tracked by an `ai:triage` GitHub issue:

| Bullet / topic | Issue | M14 task |

> **Type:** workstream tracker · **Status:** planning / discussion — *no code changes yet.* Umbrella: {{U}}
> Actionable pieces are broken out as child issues (linked below). This tracker holds the design and the open decisions.

# Goal

Replace the current **milestone** delivery model with an **Epic → Story** model, so that planning, execution, review, and closeout all key off a single, Jira-like work-item graph instead of numbered milestone folders.

# Why

Today the repo delivers via milestones:

- Docs: `docs/milestones/m1..m14/` each holding `loop-prompts.md`, `final-review.md`, `handoff.md` (+ `_templates/`, `README.md`).
- Protocol: `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, side effects, DB validation, reporting, worktree mode, secrets, Discovery/Debate Gate).
- Skills: `milestone-final-review`, `milestone-review`, `worktree-milestone-pr`.
- Agents: `milestone-closeout`, `milestone-loop-runner`, `milestone-reviewer`.

Milestones are coarse and linear. An Epic/Story model gives: a single global key across all work; explicit parent/child/dependency/blocker relationships in frontmatter; per-story readiness gating; and a clean handoff contract into the autonomous loop skills ({{T2}}).

# Proposed model

**Work items**
- **Epic** — top delivery unit. Planned; carries files + child stories. Doc: `docs/epics/kca_<n>_<slug>.md`; registry `docs/epics/README.md`; one GitHub milestone per epic.
- **Story** — a slice of an epic. Planned; carries files + Loop Prompts. Doc: `docs/stories/kca_<n>_<slug>.md`; registry `docs/stories/README.md`. Companions per story: `kca_<n>_review.md`, `docs/handoffs/kca_<n>_handoff.md`, `kca_<n>.readiness.json` (the {{T2}} handoff artifact).
- **Task / Bug** — lightweight; a GitHub issue + prompt, no doc file required.

**Keys & naming** — single global monotonic key `KCA-<n>` (decision in {{U}}); type is metadata, not baked into the number. Filename = snake_case key + slug. Story frontmatter carries `parent: KCA-<epic>`. Branch `feat/kca_<n>_<slug>`.

**Frontmatter relationship metadata** (referenced as links/paths, never pasted): `parent`, `children`, `related`, `dependencies`, `blockers`, `github_issues`, `github_prs`, `docs`, `evidence`, `external_links`, plus `implementation_status`.

**Readiness ladder** (`implementation_status`): `DOC_ONLY` (design-freeze; `/dev-loop` refuses and redirects to `/dev-plan`) → `READY_FOR_IMPL` (buildable; emits `kca_<n>.readiness.json`) → `TEST_PROVEN` → … . The human labels `ai:ready` / `decision:confirmed` are unchanged.

**Loop Prompt format** (unchanged concept from milestone mode): one scoped, independently-committable task with `Task` / `Acceptance` / `Test` / `Files (likely)`; one commit per Loop Prompt.

**GitHub linkage** — Story = issue with `type:feature|type:story` + `parent:` epic; Epic = GitHub milestone; PR closes the story issue.

# Child issues

<!-- populated after creation -->

# Open decisions (refine here)

- Key prefix `KCA-<n>` and doc dirs `docs/epics/` + `docs/stories/` (vs reusing `docs/plan/`).
- Fate of existing `docs/milestones/m1..m14` — freeze as historical vs migrate (broken out as a child issue).
- Whether to keep a lightweight "milestone" concept for anything runtime-related.

# Out of scope

- The `/dev-plan` `/dev-loop` skills themselves → {{T2}}.
- Enabling wiki/discussions → {{T4}}.

> **Type:** workstream tracker · **Status:** planning / discussion — *no code changes yet.* Umbrella: {{U}}
> Depends on Epic/Story mode ({{T1}}) for its work-item artifacts. Child issues linked below.

# Goal

Add a matched pair of Claude Code skills that run a bounded, auditable, largely-autonomous engineering loop:

- **`/dev-plan`** — turn a source (issue / PR / spec file / request pack) into a **reviewed planning PR** with registered epics/stories, a tracking issue, and (in `mode=impl`) a per-story implementation-readiness handoff.
- **`/dev-loop`** — take a locked target (issue / PR / `KCA-<epic|story>` / task file), implement it, run local validation, open a PR, run an **external review loop**, fix/rebut, and reach merge-readiness.

Both are slash-/explicit-only (`disable-model-invocation: true`), resumable from on-disk state, and use an **autonomous read-only external reviewer** where **Claude writes/fixes and the reviewer only audits** (emits `audit.json`; the orchestrator posts the audit comment on its behalf).

# How they fit this repo

- **Handoff contract:** `/dev-plan mode=impl` sets stories to `READY_FOR_IMPL` and emits `docs/stories/kca_<n>.readiness.json`; `/dev-loop` consumes it and **stops + redirects to `/dev-plan mode=impl`** if a target is `DOC_ONLY` / has no readiness artifact. This is why {{T1}} is a dependency.
- **Reviewer backend:** the repo already ships a Codex plugin (`codex:*` skills: `rescue`, `setup`, `codex-cli-runtime`, `gpt-5-4-prompting`). The loop skills should reuse it as the review backend rather than adding a parallel one. Reviewer runs read-only (`dev-plan`) or workspace-write-but-`repo_write_policy=forbidden` with post-review no-diff enforcement (`dev-loop`); never commits/pushes/merges; `danger-full-access` refused.
- **Autonomy & audit:** loops honor the existing worktree-per-unit rule, human-merge default, no push to `main`, no force-push, and the KCA vs Claude-Code-harness audit-log distinction. Overnight/daytime scheduling and per-risk loop budgets to be defined in the ported protocol.

# Artifacts each skill produces (proposed, KCA-namespaced)

- `/dev-plan`: epic/story docs + updated registries; one planning PR; at-most-one tracking issue per epic; (`mode=impl`) `kca_<n>.readiness.json` + `<epic-slug>_work_advice.md`; runtime state under `.dev-plan/state/` + artifacts under `.dev-plan/artifacts/<run_id>/`; interview scratch in `temp/` (gitignored).
- `/dev-loop`: code + tests; the PR; per-round `validation.json` / `audit.json` / `fix-disposition.json` under `.dev-loop/artifacts/pr-<pr>/r<round>/`; state under `.dev-loop/state/`; PR audit + fix-disposition comments (round-scoped markers, append-only); tracking-issue sync.
- Each skill: `SKILL.md`, `CONFIG.example.yaml`, `schemas/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`. (Structure detailed in the per-skill child issues.)

# Env-var migration — `WOS_*` → `KCA_*`

The reference design namespaces the two skills' config under `WOS_*`. **We rename to `KCA_*`** to match this repo's existing convention (`KCA_DB_TARGET`, `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE`, `KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_*`, …). Config files: `.dev-plan.yaml` / `.dev-loop.yaml` (fall back to each skill's `CONFIG.example.yaml`); syntax `${KCA_*:default}`.

**`/dev-plan` (10 vars)**

| New (`KCA_*`) | From (`WOS_*`) | Default | Controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `KCA_PLAN_MAX_REVIEW_TURNS` | `WOS_PLAN_MAX_REVIEW_TURNS` | 5 | Bound on the fix↔review loop |
| `KCA_PLAN_MAX_QUESTION_BATCH` | `WOS_PLAN_MAX_QUESTION_BATCH` | 5 | Interview question batch size |
| `KCA_PLAN_BASE_BRANCH` | `WOS_PLAN_BASE_BRANCH` | main | Planning-PR base branch |
| `KCA_PLAN_ALLOW_AUTO_MERGE` | `WOS_PLAN_ALLOW_AUTO_MERGE` | false | Enable auto-merge |
| `KCA_PLAN_ALLOW_DB_READ` | `WOS_PLAN_ALLOW_DB_READ` | true | Allow read-only DB evidence |
| `KCA_PLAN_INTERVIEW_LANG` | `WOS_PLAN_INTERVIEW_LANG` | zh | Interview scratch language (committed docs stay `en`) |
| `KCA_PLAN_REVIEWER_MODEL` | `WOS_PLAN_REVIEWER_MODEL` | (reviewer default) | External reviewer model |
| `KCA_PLAN_REVIEWER_EFFORT` | `WOS_PLAN_REVIEWER_EFFORT` | xhigh | Reviewer reasoning effort |
| `KCA_PLAN_REVIEWER_APPROVAL` | `WOS_PLAN_REVIEWER_APPROVAL` | never | Reviewer `--ask-for-approval` |
| `KCA_PLAN_REVIEWER_SANDBOX` | `WOS_PLAN_REVIEWER_SANDBOX` | read-only | Reviewer `--sandbox` |

# What

Make the harness inventory (#171) **self-maintaining** instead of hand-edited.

## Proposal

- `docs/harness/inventory.manifest.json` — curated Purpose/Status text per component (the only hand-edited surface).
- `scripts/harness/render-inventory.mjs` (or `.py`) — read the repo tree (`.claude/skills/*`, `.claude/agents/*` incl. `model:` frontmatter, `.claude/hooks/*` + `.claude/settings.json` wiring, `.github/workflows/*` triggers, `.mcp.json`) + the manifest → render the tables between `<!-- AUTO:BEGIN -->` / `<!-- AUTO:END -->` markers in issue #171.
- `.github/workflows/harness-inventory.yml` — regenerate + sync the issue body in place on push to `main` touching the harness surface, plus a weekly cron.
